observations.body: Hebrews evokes touchable mountain, fire, darkness, storm, trumpet, terrifying voice, and Moses’ fear, then contrasts Zion’s assembly, Jesus, sprinkled blood, warning, shaken creation, kingdom, worship, and consuming fire.
observations.label: The fearful mountain is contrasted with Zion and an unshakable kingdom

observations.body: The fearful mountain is contrasted with Zion and an unshakable kingdom belongs to sinai remembered in the Sinai trail.
observations.label: Where this sits

observations.body: Hebrews 12:18–29 supplies later-memory evidence for the event’s developing sequence.
observations.label: Within the Sinai event

observations.body: Later witnesses select and reuse Sinai in their own settings; they remain later readings rather than replacements for the Exodus event.
observations.label: Reading boundary

payload.posture: Read Hebrews 12:18–29 as its own source before carrying it into the wider Sinai trail.
payload.tension: The fearful mountain is contrasted with Zion and an unshakable kingdom belongs to the sinai remembered movement, but its part in the event must remain distinct from the surrounding speech, response, breach, and renewal.
payload.title: The fearful mountain is contrasted with Zion and an unshakable kingdom
